senses.gloss: f.(b. h.; ערל to hang over, v. Ges. Thes. s. v. ערל) [sheath,] prepuce; the uncircumcised membrum.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 46:13">Gen. R. s. 46</cite> <he>עָרְלַת הגוף</he> the foreskin of the membrum.
<cite ref="Shabbat 134b:23">Sabb. 134ᵇ</cite>, sq. <he>עָרְלתוֹ ודאי דוחה את השבת</he> the cutting of his prepuce, where there is no doubt (about the condition of the infant), supersedes the Sabbath.

<cite ref="Pesachim 92a:8">Pes. 92ᵃ</cite> <he>הפורש מן הע׳ וכ׳</he> he who separates himself from the prepuce (a gentile converted and circumcised) is like one that separates himself from a grave (has to undergo the lustrations of one that has been in contact with a corpse).
Ned. III, 11 שאין הע׳ קרויה אלא לשמם for ʿorlah (the word ʿărelim) is used only as a general name for gentiles, v. עָרֵל.

<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 3:11">Ib.</cite> <he>מאוסה</he> (<he>היא ה</he>)<he>ע׳ שנתגנו וכ׳</he> uncircumcision is detestable, for it is applied to the wicked as a reproach (with ref. to <cite ref="Jeremiah 9:25">Jer. IX, 25</cite>); a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="P01388"><he>עֲרָלוֹת</he></cite>, constr. <cite ref="P01388"><he>עָרְלוֹת</he></cite>.

Yeb. 72ᵃ; Sabb. 135ᵇ מי שיש לו שתי ע׳ if one has two prepuces; (oth. opin. two membra to be circumcised). Gen. G. s. 46, a. e. ארבע ע׳ הן וכ׳ the term ʿorlah (uncircumcision) is applied in four ways; a. fr.—Trnsf. (v.
Lev. XIX, 23) [that which is to be rejected,] the fruit of trees of the first three years.
Orl. I, 2 חייב בע׳ is subject to the law of ʿorlah.
Ib. 6 נטיעה של ע׳ a young tree subject to the law of ʿorlah.
<cite ref="Mishnah Orlah 1:7">Ib. 7</cite> <he>שרף הע׳</he> resin of a young tree; a. fr.—
Tosef. Ter. V, 9, a. fr. עוֹרְלָה.—ʿOrlah, name of a treatise of Mishnah, Tosefta and Talmud Y’rushalmi, of the Order of Z’raʿim.
